sentences.text: This case is registered against the accused for the offence punishable under Section 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act (in brief N.I.Act for brevity).

2. The substance of the case of complainant :
It is the case of the complainant that the accused borrowed loan of Rs.2,00,000/-
from the complainant on 27.05.2019 by executing relevant documents.
The accused became defaulter.

After several demands, the accused issued cheque of Canara Bank,
Magadi Road Branch, Bengaluru, bearing No.662599 dated 20.05.2023 for Rs.99,420/- to discharge his liability.

3. The complainant presented the said cheque through his banker Karnataka Bank Ltd.,
Rajarajeshwarinagar branch, Bengaluru for realization.
It was dishonored for the reason funds insufficient on 26.05.2023.
Thereafter, he issued legal notice to the accused through registered post on 21.06.2023 by calling upon him to make payment within 15 days.
The said notice was served.
The accused neither replied nor made payment of said amount.
The accused knowingly issued a cheque with an intention to cause loss to complainant.
The said amount is legally recoverable debt.

Hence,
KABC030511252023 complainant prays to punish the accused for the offence under Section 138 of N.I. Act.
4.
After receiving the complaint this Court scrutinized the documents.
Sworn statement of the complainant was recorded.
He filed his sworn statement by way of affidavit.
There were sufficient materials to constitute the offence.
Hence, this Court took cognizance for an offence under Section 138 of N.I. Act and issued process against the accused.
5. Secured the presence of accused.
He was enlarged on bail.
The substance of accusation was read over to accused in the language known to him, for which he pleaded not guilty.

6. As per the guidelines issued by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Indian Bank Association Vs.
Union of India & others reported in 2014(5) SCC 590 this Court treated the sworn statement of complainant as evidence.

sentences.text: This Court also recorded the statement of accused under Section 313 of Cr.P.C.
The accused denied the incriminating evidence of complainant and chose to lead defence evidence.
Thereafter, the counsel for complainant was seeking permission to represent the complainant through new authorized person since, the earlier representative had resigned to his job.
Thereafter, new authorized person examined himself as PW-2.
The accused cross-examined the PW-2.

Further, he examined himself as DW-1.
KABC030511252023 7.
Heard both side.
Perused the materials placed on record.

The following points arise for my consideration.

1. Whether complainant proves beyond all reasonable doubt that the accused towards discharge of his liability issued cheque bearing No.662599 dated 20.05.2023 for Rs.99,420/- drawn on Canara Bank, Magadi Road branch, Bengaluru in his favour and when he presented the said cheque for realization, it was dishonored for the reason funds insufficient in the account maintained by the accused?
2. Whether the complainant proves beyond all reasonable doubt that he issued demand notice to the accused, the accused did not repay the cheque amount within statutory period and thereby he has committed an offence punishable U/Sec.138 of N.I.Act?
3. What order?
9.
My answers to the above points as under.
Point No.1 & 2 : In the Affirmative.

Point No.3 : As per final order, for the following:
REASONS 10.
POINT NO.1 and 2 :
These points are inter-linked with each other, to avoid repetition of facts and circumstances they are taken together for common discussion.
To substantiate the case against accused, the complainant relied on documents which were marked as Ex.P1 to 10.
The PW-1 who is authorized person of complainant reiterated the averments of complaint in his evidence.
The Ex.P1 is cheque.
Ex . P2
is memo issued by the banker.
It shows that when complainant presented the Ex.P1 cheque for realization, it was dishonored on 26.05.2023 for the reason funds insufficient.
Ex.P3 is office copy of the legal notice.
Ex.P4 is postal receipt.
Ex . P5
is postal acknowledgment.
These documents show that complainant issued notice to the accused on 21.06.2023 i.e., within 30 days from the date of dishonor of cheque by calling upon him to pay cheque amount within 15 days.
The accused had not paid the amount of cheque to the complainant within 15 days from the date of service of notice.
Ex.P6 is authorization letter.
Ex.P7 is loan application.
Ex.P8 is sanction order.
Ex.P9 is loan agreement and Ex.P10 is guarantee agreement.

The evidence and documents clearly indicate that the complainant complied the ingredients to constitute an offence punishable under Section 138 of N.I.Act.
12.
The N.I. Act provides some presumptions in favour of complainant under Section 118 and 139 of N.I. Act.

Under Section 118 of N.I. Act, there is a presumption that until the contrary is proved,

Even under Section 139 of N.I. Act, it is specifically stated that it shall be presumed, unless the contrary is proved, that the holder of KABC030511252023 a cheque received the cheque for discharge, in whole or in part, of any debt or other liability.
However, it is well settled principle of law that the said presumption can be rebutted by accused by raising probable defence.
13. In order to rebut the presumption the accused has to cross-examine the complainant and lead defence evidence.
In the present case, the accused cross-
examined the PW-2 and examined himself as DW-1.
In the present case, issuance of cheque, signature in cheque and loan transaction are admitted facts.
The defence of accused is, he gave Ex.P1 cheque at the time of borrowing loan for the purpose of security to loan.
The accused further contended that notice is not served on him.

Hence,
complaint is not maintainable.
14. The counsel for accused elaborately cross-examined the PW-2.
The PW-2 deposed in his cross-examination that the accused applied for loan of Rs.2,00,000/-.
After deducting processing fee of Rs.13,000/- the complainant gave loan amount to the accused.
The handwriting in Ex.P1 cheque belongs to him.
His higher authority stated him about the balance of accused.
Further the counsel for accused had put suggestion that complainant misused the Ex.P1 cheque which was given for the purpose of security to loan.
The PW-2 denied the same as false.
The PW-2 further deposed that when he issued notice for repayment of loan, then KABC030511252023 accused gave Ex.P1 cheque for repayment of loan.
He received cheque from the accused at the time of borrowing loan.
15. The accused examined himself as DW-1.
He deposed that he applied for loan of Rs.2,00,000/- in the year 2019.
After deducting processing fee of Rs.20,000/- they gave Rs.1,80,000/-.

At that time,
the complainant received 5 empty cheques from him.
Thereafter, he repaid 5-6 EMIs.

Thereafter,
due to financial crisis he did not pay further EMIs.
The notice issued by the complainant was not served on him.
He had not mentioned the details in Ex.P1 cheque.
The counsel for complainant cross-examined the DW.1.
The DW.1 clearly admitted that the address mentioned in notice and postal acknowledgment belongs to him.
16. The defense of accused is, notice issued by the complainant was not served on him.
Ex.P3 is office copy of legal notice.
Ex . P4
is postal receipt.
Ex . P5
is postal acknowledgment.

The DW-1 clearly admitted in his cross-examination at para 9 that the address mentioned in Ex.P5 postal acknowledgment belongs to him and he had not given any complaint to the police by stating that some one has received notice on his behalf.
These facts clearly show that the complainant issued notice to the correct address of accused.
If the signature which is appearing in Ex.P5 postal acknowledgment not belongs to the accused, his family member might have received the same.
Moreover, it is not the case of KABC030511252023 accused that he was residing in some other address as on the date of notice.
If accused had taken the defence of non-service of notice, he has to establish that he was residing in some other address as on the date of issuance of notice.
He has to produce documentary evidence in this regard.
But the accused has not produced any documents in this regard.
Moreover, the accused himself admitted in his cross-examination that the address mentioned in Ex.P5 postal acknowledgment belongs to him.
It clearly shows that notice is duly served on family member of accused.

sentences.text: At this stage, I would like to refer the decision of Larger Bench of Hon'ble Apex Court published in (2007) 6 SCC 555 between C.C.Alavi Haji Vs Palapetty Muhammed wherein the larger bench of Hon'ble Apex court clearly held that it is the duty of complainant to send statutory notice to the correct address of accused.
Whether the said notice was returned as unserved as unclaimed or refused etc., it is deemed to be served on accused as per section 27 of The General Clauses Act.
In the present case, the complainant discharged his duty by sending statutory notice to the correct address of accused.
Moreover, postal acknowledgment clearly shows that someone received the said notice.
Hence, it clearly shows that the notice issued by the complainant was served on accused.
. The accused further contended that he had given Ex.P1 cheque for the purpose of security to loan at the time of borrowing loan.
He had not given Ex.P1 cheque for repayment of loan.
It is well settled law that the complainant can use the cheque which was given for the purpose of security, for repayment of loan.
In the present case, the DW-1 clearly deposed in his chief-examination at para 3 that after payment of 5-6 EMIs, he stopped to pay EMIs due to financial crisis.
It shows that the accused was defaulter in payment of installments.
Moreover, after taking loan in the year 2019 he repaid only 5-6 EMIs.
Thereafter, till today he has not paid any EMIs.
The said situation clearly creates right to complainant to use the cheque which was given for the purpose to security to loan.
Moreover, the accused has not taken any criminal action against complainant for misusing the said cheque.
There is no illegality in using the cheque which was given for the purpose of security.
19. The accused further contended that except his signature in Ex.P1 cheque other entries were not made by him.
The PW-2 himself admitted that he wrote the said entries.

At this situation, I would like to refer the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court published in (2019) 4 SCC 197 between Bir Singh Vs Mukesh Kumar, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court clearly held that once the accused admitted the issuance of cheque and signature in cheque for some consideration, who wrote the cheque is immaterial and the court KABC030511252023 shall presume that the said entries were made in the presence of accused as per directions of accused.
In the present case, issuance of cheque and signature is admitted by the accused.
Hence, the handwriting of PW-2 in Ex.P1 cheque will not invalidate the case of complainant.
20. The accused further contended that he applied for loan for Rs.2,00,000/-.
But the complainant after deducting processing fee of Rs.20,000/- issued Rs.1,80,000/- only.
The PW-1 also admitted that after deducting processing charge of Rs.13,000/-, he gave rest of the amount as loan.
These facts clearly show that the complainant issued loan amount of Rs.2,00,000/- and deduct the processing fee.
In this regard, the accused has not produced any documents to show that the complainant had given Rs.1,80,000/- only.
The amount was transferred to his account.
The accused has not produced statement of account to show the same.
It is admitted fact that loan of Rs.2,00,000/- was granted and in said amount processing fee was deducted.
There is no illegality.
If loan of Rs.2,00,000/- was not granted, then matter would be the different.
Hence, this defence is also not acceptable one.

sentences.text: Once the execution of Negotiable Instrument is either proved or admitted, then the Court shall draw a presumption to the effect that Negotiable Instrument has been drawn for valid consideration and legally recoverable debt was in existence.
Hence, KABC030511252023 this court considered that there is legally recoverable debt and the accused issued Ex.P1 cheque in favour of complainant to discharge his liability.
The accused failed to prove his burden.
In the present case, the complainant proved that the accused has committed an offence punishable under section 138 of N.I. Act.
Hence, I answer the point No.1 and 2 in the Affirmative.
22. Point No.3:

Once the accused is found guilty for the offence punishable under section 138 of N.I.Act, he may be punished with imprisonment for a term which may be extended to two years or with fine which may be extended to twice of the amount of the cheque or with both.

At this stage I would like to refer the decision published in 2011 Cr.L.J. 2593 between Koushalya Devi Massand Vs.
Roopkishore Khore, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court held that since offence under N.I.Act is civil wrong, the gravity of complaint can not be equated with the offence of Indian Penal Code and instead of jail sentence, impose of fine payable as compensation is found sufficient to metes ends of justice.

entities.text:
Koushalya Devi Massand Vs.
Roopkishore Khore
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, it is just and proper to impose sentence of fine on the accused instead of sentence to send him to jail.

23. As per Sec.357(1)(b) of Code of Criminal Procedure, when Court imposes sentence of fine on the accused, may order the whole or any part of fine to be applied in the payment to any person of compensation for any loss or injury caused by the offence.
In the present case the complainant is society.
The amount involved in this case is public money.
The complainant suffered loss by the reason of the act of the accused.
The accused issued cheque in the month of May, 2023.
If the accused paid said amount on that time, certainly the complainant would have get some benefits by this time.
Hence, it is proper to impose reasonable fine against the accused.
Cheque amount is Rs.99,420/-.
Imposing fine of Rs.1,50,000/- become reasonable fine.

Hence, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
Acting under Section 255(2) of Cr.P.C. the accused is convicted for the offence punishable under Section 138 of N.I.Act and sentenced to pay fine of Rs.1,50,000/- (One lakh fifty thousand only).
The accused is directed to pay the said fine amount on or before 30 days from today.
In default of payment of fine amount, the accused shall under go simple imprisonment for six months.

If fine is realized, Rs.1,45,000/- shall be paid to the complainant as compensation as per Section 357 of Cr.P.C. and remaining Rs.5,000/- shall be paid towards the State as fine for incurring prosecution expenses.
